prior_importants.description: `targetHolds` calls `git ls-tree` without `--full-tree`, so a session that plants `core.worktree` in the shared `.git/config` narrows the listing to nothing; `targetHolds` returns `[]` and the gate falls back to the pre-157 fail-open, judging an existing file the before-measure omits against the cap of 50 instead of the +15 rise.

findings.description: In ADR 0157's rule paragraph, the `--full-tree` aside now sits in the middle of the rule. That leaves "It keeps the paths that list holds out of the changed paths plus every rename or copy pair's source" with "It" pointing at `core.worktree`, and "keeps … out of" reads as dropping the held paths. Move the aside after the sentence and say the gate keeps the changed paths and pair sources that the listing holds.

ADR 0157's *Tests.* paragraph leaves out the new merge-gate test ("reads the target tree whole when the shared config aims core.worktree elsewhere"). That test is the only guard for the rule paragraph's `--full-tree` claim. Add one sentence saying a session-written `core.worktree` of `/` still flags the existing file at +20.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer could not run `scripts/adr-index.sh` under the CI command lock, so it did not check ADR 0157's number against the generated index. It also reported that it never read `debt.test.ts` or `merge-gate.test.ts` against `docs/conventions/testing.md`, so those test files got only the correctness reviewer's behavioural check.
